title: Marketplace publish safety and asset acceptance blueprint
content:
Purpose: quick reference playbook for safe publish of a new Redwood product tile across cloud marketplaces (AWS/GCP/Azure) and partner portals. This is intentionally pragmatic -- a checklist + accept/reject criteria + short creative specs so product, legal, and ops can sign off quickly.

Context and audience:
- Audience: GTM launch lead, marketplace ops engineer, partner success, legal reviewer, content designer.
- Use-case: early-stage listing (beta or GA) where we must validate legal, security, billing mapping, UX assets, and regional compliance before scheduling an automated publish.
- Not a replacement for legal counsel; meant to reduce obvious rework and failed publishes.

Quick summary (1-line): must pass all safety checks OR have an approved mitigation plan before pushing to production marketplaces.

1) Pre-publish acceptance matrix (hard gates) -- every item must be YES or a linked mitigation ticket
- Product description: accurate, short (<=280 chars) + long description (<=2000 chars) present. No claims of regulatory compliance unless validated. (Accept if: no regulatory claims or legal sign-off).
- Data handling disclosure: clear statement on customer data retention/opt-out for logs. (Accept if: statement exists OR private deployment only flag set).
- PII / sensitive output guidance: included in FAQ or usage guidance. (Accept if: guidance included or model restricted to internal tiers).
- Security checklist: penetration test report or internal SRE sign-off within last 12 months for private/dedicated; hosted API needs documented least-privilege notes. (Accept if: sign-off present).
- Billing SKU mapping: sku_id + pricing tier + trial credit flag mapped to cloud ledger. (Accept if: finance mapped and validated with BillingOps).
- Support path and SLO: public contact + escalation documented. (Accept if: contact and SLO page link).
- Copyright and IP: no unlicensed third-party content used in marketing images or copy. (Accept if: license verified).
- Legal clause: export controls / embargoes checked for target regions (APAC variants). (Accept if: legal OK).

2) Creative & asset acceptance (visual spec + copy variants) -- keep assets small and modular
- Tile title: 6 words max, primary benefit first. Example: "Redwood Inference — Low-latency LLM API" (short).
- One-line subtitle (tile blurb): 10–14 words. Avoid platform-specific comparisons.
- Long summary: 3 short paragraphs (what it does, who it's for, getting started bullet).
- CTA copy: "Start free trial", "Request demo", or "Contact sales" (one only).
- Screenshots: provide 2 variants: console view and sample API call. PNG, 1920x1080 and 1200x628 (social). No mocked PII. Annotate with captions.
- Logo: SVG + 1 raster fallback, transparent bg, 600x600 px recommended. Colors: follow brand palette.
- Icon/tile image: avoid faces; abstract/data-centric imagery preferred for marketplaces. If faces used, have model releases.
- Localization: supply translated title + subtitle + long summary for en-US, en-GB, fr-FR, de-DE, ja-JP, ko-KR, zh-CN. If not available at publish, mark limited locales in metadata.

3) Acceptance checklist for technical gating (ops/infra)
- Verified endpoint URLs and health checks (staging & prod).
- Rate limit and quota defaults set (tenant-level overrides documented).
- Model variant fallbacks defined (e.g., fallback to smaller quantized model on capacity events).
- Logs & telemetry: masked for PII, retention policy inline (30/90/365 days options) and mapped to customer's plan.
- Key management: KMS integration path described for Private customers.
- VPC / network requirements: firewall or allowed IP ranges documented for Dedicated/Private.

4) Billing & SKU mapping notes (finance ops)
- SKU naming convention: RED-<PRODUCT>-<TIER>-<REGION>. Example: RED-INFER-API-PRO-US.
- Trial vs paid: trial duration (14 days) and token cap. Confirmed trial credit bucket: TRIAL_2026_Q1.
- Marketplace cut impacts: ensure list price accounts for marketplace fee (e.g., AWS listing -> 20% markup to preserve net).
- Metering event definitions: token vs embedding units vs request-minutes. Map to cloud usage metric id.

5) Localization & APAC-specific cautions
- Content review: avoid country-specific compliance claims (e.g., 'China-ready') unless infra is validated.
- Language tone: Japanese copy must be formal; translate by in-house LATAM translators or approved vendor.
- Payment flow differences: ensure marketplace billing supports local currencies or mark as USD-only.

6) Rollout plan & guardrails (recommended phased approach)
- Phase A (beta): 10 partners, limited quota, monitor latency and usage patterns for 2 weeks.
- Phase B (regional): enable 1-2 additional regions (EU or APAC) after beta stability.
- Phase C (public GA): broad availability after SLAs met for 30 days.
- Feature flags: publish should set a soft-gate tag so we can rollback via marketplace metadata within 24 hours.

7) Rollback / incident playbook highlights
- If model outputs show elevated hallucination or safety regressions (user complaints >= X/day or quality alert threshold), unpublish tile and route customers to fallback variant.
- If billing discrepancy detected, pause new signups and notify BillingOps within 4 hours.
- Contact matrix: GTM lead -> Marketplace Ops -> SRE -> Legal -> CS. Provide Slack channel and incident runbook link.

8) Sample copy snippets (short):
- Tile title (US): "Redwood Inference — Predictable, low-cost LLM serving"
- Tile blurb: "Ship LLM features with predictable latency and observable cost controls. Start free."
- Long summary opening: "Redwood Inference provides a production-first LLM inference platform — hosted API, dedicated capacity, and private deployments — so engineering teams deliver reliable LLM features at predictable costs."

9) Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self style)
- Confirm APAC regional availability for private deployments with infra team (ticket: INFRA-1291).
- Get final legal wording for data residency for Japan and Korea.
- Finalize translated assets with vendor (ETA 2026-03-20).

10) Owner & sign-off matrix (who stamps OK)
- Product GTM (owner): Maya Chen — overall approval for copy and rollout.
- Marketplace Ops: Diego Alvarez — technical and publish readiness.
- Legal: Priya Patel — IP/data/export compliance.
- Finance/Billing: Liam O'Connor — sku and price mapping.

Appendix: quick links
- Marketplace guidelines (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GT/Marketplace+Catalog+Governance
- Sandbox listing PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-assets/pull/78
- Billing ticket: JIRA GTM-842

Version notes: first draft, aiming for a single page actionable checklist. Keep this doc as the canonical lightweight gate; move final copy and assets into the repo under /marketplace-assets once signed off.
